text.p: Australia are facing a bowling crisis as they prepare for next week's first cricket test against West Indies after paceman Glenn McGrath joined a growing list of casualties on Friday.
McGrath, Australia's new ball strike bowler, was forced to pull out of a domestic four-day match starting on Friday because of a badly-blistered callous of the left heel.
His withdrawal came only 24 hours after fellow test paceman Damien Fleming was sidelined with a thigh muscle strain.

With concern still surrounding the fitness of leg-spinner Shane Warne, Australia are facing the prospect of fielding a severely weakened bowling attack in the Brisbane test, starting at the Gabba on November 22.
Veteran fast bowler Craig McDermott has already ruled himself out of the first matches in the five-test series against West Indies because of a knee injury.

McGrath, who will miss New South Wales' Sheffield Shield match against Queensland in Sydney, said the injury has been troubling him for several weeks and prompted him to take pain-killers during the recent tour to India.
"When I come down on it (during the delivery stride) it's like someone jabbing a needle in my heel," McGrath told Friday's Sydney Morning Herald newspaper.
Fast bowlers Michael Kasprowicz, Anthony Stuart and Andrew Bichel are regarded as the most likely candidates to fill any vacancies in Australia's pace attack next week.
Warne, Australia's most potent bowler in recent years, has yet to prove his complete recovery from surgery to the ring finger of his bowling hand.
In Hobart, West Indies on Friday began a four-day match against an Australian XI, the tourists' final warm-up match before the first test match.
